content.title: Oscars 2026: Surprise Tie In Short Film Category
content.text: Advertisement Dismiss Ad Dismiss Adby Natasha JokicBuzzFeedBuzzFeed StaffI'm a Senior Staff Writer at BuzzFeed covering pop culture, entertainment, and politics. 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Believe it or not, there was a tie at the 2026 Oscars. ABC Advertisement A tie is so rare that it's only happened six times before. The most recent tie occurred in 2013 in the Sound Editing Category, when both Zero Dark Thirty (Paul N. J. Ottosson) and Skyfall (Per Hallberg and Karen Baker Landers) won. Oscars are voted on by online ballots of eligible members, so a tie isn't impossible. Oscars This year, Kumail Nanjiani presented the Oscar for Best Live Action Short Film. Except when it came to opening the envelope, he looked more surprised than you might expect: ABC Advertisement "And the Oscar goes to... It's a tie. I'm not joking," he said. "Everyone calm down, we're going to get through this. Focus up." ABC The first Oscar was for The Singers, which was won by Sam A. Davis and Jack Piatt. Fittingly, when Sam got to the stage, he said, "A tie, wow. I didn't know that was a thing." ABC Advertisement "Ironic that the Short Film Oscar is going to take twice as long," Kumail then said, before Two People Exchanging Saliva was announced as the second winner. ABC "We are so happy to be sharing this Oscar with The Singers, we love all our fellow nominees," director and writer Natalie Musteata said once she got on stage. ABC Advertisement History in the making, folks! Check out the rest of our Oscars coverage here.
